explanations.explanation: Moses it is, friend. The Levite heads say it plainly: "The LORD commanded through Moses that we be given cities in which to live…" (Joshua 21:2). Moses was Israel's leader before Joshua. They aren't asking for a favor here. They're pointing to a command that was already given.

Aaron's a fair guess, since he's the priest everybody connects with the Levites. Aaron was Moses' brother and Israel's first high priest (Exodus 28:1). But the Levite heads say the LORD commanded "through Moses" (Joshua 21:2). Aaron's family does show up later in the passage, so keep him close.

Samuel, the prophet, is a little early for this scene, friend. He doesn't show up in the Bible until way later, in 1 Samuel. In this passage the Levite heads say the LORD commanded "through Moses" (Joshua 21:2). Moses is the one who led Israel before Joshua.

Cities to live in. The Levite heads say the LORD commanded "that we be given cities in which to live…" (Joshua 21:2). The Levites don't get a big plot of their own. They get homes spread out among the other tribes. That's a whole lot of houses, baker.

Tents near the tabernacle is a good guess, because the Levites did camp around it in the wilderness (Numbers 1:53). But the Levites aren't asking for tents here. They say the LORD commanded that they be given "cities in which to live" (Joshua 21:2). The tents days are over, and they're moving into real addresses.

explanations.answer: A share of the war spoils
explanations.explanation: War spoils is a creative pick, friend. But nothing in this request mentions spoils. The Levite heads say the LORD's command was for "cities in which to live, together with pasturelands for our livestock" (Joshua 21:2). The Levites are asking for places to live, not loot.

Pasturelands is right. The Levite heads ask for cities "together with pasturelands for our livestock" (Joshua 21:2). Animals need grass, and grass needs room. Even I know you can't keep a herd in a cookie jar.

Storehouses sound sensible, since you have to put things somewhere. But the Levites ask for "pasturelands for our livestock" (Joshua 21:2). Livestock need open ground to graze, not a building to sit in. I can't even keep my cookie boxes in order, so let's leave the herd to the experts.

Stables is close, since stables are where animals sleep. But the Levites ask for "pasturelands for our livestock" (Joshua 21:2). That's open land for grazing, not a building with a roof. A stable might be nice, but grass is what they asked for.

explanations.answer: They give cities out of their own land
explanations.explanation: That's right, baker. The text says the Israelites gave the Levites these cities and pasturelands "out of their own inheritance" (Joshua 21:3). It also says they did it "by the command of the LORD." Nobody argues and nobody stalls. Each tribe just hands some over.

explanations.answer: They tell the Levites to wait a year
explanations.explanation: Nobody tells the Levites to wait, friend. Joshua 21:3 says the Israelites gave the cities "by the command of the LORD." Then the lots start coming out right away. No waiting room, no number to take.

explanations.answer: They point them to land not yet conquered
explanations.explanation: That would be like handing someone a coupon for a cookie that isn't baked yet. But verse 3 says the tribes gave the Levites these cities "out of their own inheritance." The cities come from land the tribes already hold. No pointing at the horizon here.
All of it, baker. The text says, "Thus the LORD gave Israel all the land He had sworn to give their fathers…" (Joshua 21:43). Not a piece of it, not most of it. All of it.

Most of it sounds humble and reasonable, but the text goes further. It says the LORD gave Israel "all the land He had sworn to give their fathers…" (Joshua 21:43). That word "all" is right there in the verse. I almost never get "all" out of my own cookie batches, so this one stands out.

Half is a big step down from what the verse says. Joshua 21:43 says the LORD gave Israel "all the land He had sworn to give their fathers…" All of it, not a half. If I only got half the dough I ordered, I'd be a very sad stamper.
True. The verse says Israel "took possession of it and settled in it" (Joshua 21:43). They got the land, and then they unpacked. That's a good feeling for any family, after all the moving around.

This one is true, friend. Joshua 21:43 says that after the LORD gave Israel the land, "they took possession of it and settled in it." So the land wasn't just handed over and left sitting there. Israel moved in and settled.

Rest is right. "And the LORD gave them rest on every side, just as He had sworn to their fathers" (Joshua 21:44). On every side, baker. That's the kind of rest I dream about after a full day of stamping.

Walls make sense when you think about enemies. But the verse says, "the LORD gave them rest on every side…" (Joshua 21:44). What He gave was rest, not something built. Rest is a gift, and this one came with a promise behind it.

Allies sounds like a smart way to handle enemies, friend. But Joshua 21:44 says, "the LORD gave them rest on every side…" The verse doesn't mention friends coming to help. It names rest, and it says the LORD gave it.

explanations.answer: The LORD handed them all over to Israel
explanations.explanation: That's it. The verse says, "the LORD delivered all their enemies into their hand" (Joshua 21:44). So none of them could stand against Israel. The credit goes to the LORD.

explanations.answer: Israel's army had grown too big to beat
explanations.explanation: A big army is a good guess, but the text doesn't say that. It says none of Israel's enemies could stand against them "for the LORD delivered all their enemies into their hand" (Joshua 21:44). The reason is what the LORD did. The size of the army never comes up.

explanations.answer: Their enemies had all fled the land
explanations.explanation: Running away would sure make things quiet, friend. But the verse doesn't say the enemies fled. It says, "the LORD delivered all their enemies into their hand" (Joshua 21:44). That's the reason the text gives.
Not quite, baker. Joshua 21:45 says, "Not one of all the LORD's good promises to the house of Israel had failed; everything was fulfilled." Not a few and not one. Every promise came through.

False is right. The verse says, "Not one of all the LORD's good promises to the house of Israel had failed; everything was fulfilled" (Joshua 21:45). Not one, baker. I've had a lot of cookie batches fall apart on me, so a record like that is something.
